---
title: "surveyframe and Qualtrics"
description: "How surveyframe relates to Qualtrics: what each does, what surveyframe adds for research, and how to analyse Qualtrics responses with surveyframe."
---

Qualtrics is a commercial survey platform with free and paid options. Its data export gives each answer as a numeric value, the default, or as the choice text.

surveyframe is a free R package (MIT, on CRAN) for the whole research workflow around a survey: the questionnaire and its analysis plan, the collection, the checks, the planned analyses and the APA 7 report.

## What surveyframe adds for research

- An analysis plan written before the data, with hypotheses and decision
  rules, saved in the questionnaire file.
- A pre-analysis plan to submit to OSF, Zenodo or an ethics committee.
- A hash anyone can check at [surveyframe.org/verify](https://surveyframe.org/verify/),
  and amendments recorded with their reasons.
- Quality checks, scale reliability, the planned analyses and a report in
  APA 7, in SurveyStudio or in R.

## Using Qualtrics with surveyframe

You can collect responses with Qualtrics and analyse them with surveyframe. Describe the questionnaire as a surveyframe instrument, then prepare the export so that `read_responses()` can check it against the instrument:

1. Export the responses as a CSV file. Use numeric values, and give each choice the value of its code in the instrument, or change the values after export.
2. Keep the header row and remove the descriptive rows below it, such as the row of full question text, so the first data row is the first respondent.
3. Name each column by the matching item id.
4. Declare any column outside the instrument, such as the response id or the time of submission, in `meta_cols`.

```r
raw <- read.csv("answers.csv", check.names = FALSE)
raw <- raw[-(1:2), ]  # the descriptive rows below the header: count them in your own export
names(raw) <- c("submitted", "visit_type", "satisfaction")  # each column named by its item id, in order
raw$visit_type <- c("First visit" = "first", "Returning" = "returning")[raw$visit_type]  # answer text to choice codes, where needed
responses <- read_responses(raw, instrument, meta_cols = c("submitted"))
results <- run_analysis_plan(responses, instrument)
```

The planned analyses and the report then run on these responses.
